clue.text: Put away the cards and get ready for action

definitions.meaning: decks are packs of playing cards, so clearing them away tidies up the card table
the naval idiom for removing everything from a ship's deck before battle

explanation.surface: A card game is abandoned as everyone prepares for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from warships cleared for battle, hence preparing to act; literally it also means removing packs of cards.

clue.text: Unpaid foreign noble cut no ice

definitions.meaning: a count is a continental nobleman, and one working unpaid does so for no money
idiom for having no influence or importance

explanation.surface: An aristocrat working for free makes no impression on anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of no weight or effect is the idiom; read literally it is a European nobleman with no wages.

clue.text: Sprightly fellow in river standing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, something standing up reads from the bottom upwards, so the letters are turned round
the fellow is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Nile, the African river

explanation.surface: A lively man is standing upright in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside NILE to make NIFLE, and 'standing up' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small, delicate and lively like an elf, so it is a synonym for sprightly.

clue.text: Disapprove of professional being retained by an allowance

indicators.note: the professional is held within the allowance, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rebate is an allowance or deduction from a payment
pro is the short form of professional

explanation.surface: A professional on an allowance is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to condemn or reject strongly, a formal synonym of disapprove of.

clue.text: A small bunch that's difficult to control

definitions.meaning: as much as a hand can hold, a small number
a person, often a child, who is troublesome to manage

explanation.surface: A small group turns out to be unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small quantity, as much as one hand holds, and an unruly person or thing.

clue.text: Groom's costume

definitions.meaning: to groom is to tidy and prepare

explanation.surface: The bridegroom's outfit at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the man at a wedding, but it is the verb meaning to make neat; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to prepare or tidy, as one dresses a wound or hair; a costume is clothing, a frock.

clue.text: She tries to catch your eye on the front

definitions.text: She tries to catch your eye on the front

parts.words: She tries to catch your eye on the front
parts.note: suggests a woman flirting on a seaside promenade, but the front is a magazine's front page

explanation.surface: A woman trying to attract attention while strolling along the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: A model photographed for a magazine's front page, whose job is to draw buyers' attention.

clue.text: Ceremony in which girl may be expecting to take part

definitions.text: Ceremony in which girl may be expecting to take part

parts.words: Ceremony in which girl may be expecting to take part
parts.note: expecting reads as anticipating but means pregnant: a wedding forced on a couple because the bride is pregnant

explanation.surface: A girl looks forward to taking part in a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding hastily arranged because the bride is pregnant, the father notionally forced at gunpoint.

clue.text: Polish fan

definitions.meaning: to polish is to shine up a surface
an enthusiast, as in a film devotee

explanation.surface: A supporter from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the clue is capitalised to suggest the nationality; it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rub to a shine and also an enthusiast or devotee.

clue.text: Change not initially represented before D-day

definitions.text: Change not initially represented before D-day

parts.words: Change not initially represented before D-day
parts.note: D-day here is Decimal Day, 1971; before it these coins were written with a d, not their initial letter p

explanation.surface: Some change in the plans was not shown before the wartime invasion day.
explanation.walkthrough: D-day looks like the 1944 landings, but it is Britain's Decimal Day in 1971, when the old penny abbreviation d gave way to p.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coins are loose change; before decimalisation they were abbreviated d (Latin denarius) rather than by their own first letter.

clue.text: Short book, one of a number written about one instrument

indicators.note: the volume abbreviation is written around the second one, enclosing it

parts.words: Short book, one of a number
parts.note: vol is the short form of volume, one book in a numbered set
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slim volume in a series is written about an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A viol is a bowed stringed instrument of the Renaissance, ancestor of the viola da gamba family.

clue.text: Put up with substandard footballer

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
food or a performance that is off is not up to standard

explanation.surface: Someone has to tolerate a poor-quality player.
explanation.walkthrough: A stand-off (half) is a rugby union or league position, rugby being football in the older broad sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, the stand-off half is the player between scrum-half and the three-quarters, also called fly-half.

clue.text: Shoots derogatory young men

definitions.meaning: small twigs or stems of a plant
a dismissive old word for youths, offspring of a family

explanation.surface: Someone fires at insulting youths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' looks like a verb about firing, but it is the plural noun for young growths.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stems of a plant are its young growths; the same word is a contemptuous term for callow youths.

clue.text: Obtrusive caller demonstrating hearing aid

parts.note: loud can mean showy or obtrusive, as in loud clothes
someone who hails is calling out to another

explanation.surface: A noisy shouter shows off an aid for the deaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing aid' suggests a device for the deaf, but here it is a device that helps people hear a speaker far off.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone amplifies a voice so a crowd can hear it, wittily called an aid to hearing.

clue.text: Abandoned poor Hecuba, almost dead

indicators.note: poor signals that the queen's name and the shortened word are in a bad state, rearranged together

parts.note: the queen of Troy, used just for her letters

indicators.note: dead is nearly complete but missing one letter, its A

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: The tragic Trojan queen Hecuba, deserted and close to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' here removes a middle letter rather than the usual last one: DED, which 'poor' mixes with HECUBA. 'Abandoned' looks like deserted but means dissolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned in the sense of wanton or dissolute is a synonym for morally corrupted, given over to vice.

clue.text: Gunners, sappers, fliers — all exceptional people

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
birds are creatures that fly

explanation.surface: Soldiers and airmen are all outstanding people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase rara avis, a rare bird, names an unusual person, someone uncommon.

clue.text: Drinking places where DJ must keep off spirits

indicators.note: the disc jockey has to stay away, so his letters are removed

parts.note: djinns are spirits of Arabian legend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bar where the disc jockey has to stay off the hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests strong drink in a bar scene, but it is the genies of Arabian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and hostelries are places where people go for a drink.

clue.text: Slap in the face (or nose, sort of)

definitions.meaning: a rebuff or insult, a figurative slap
a short, turned-up nose is described by this word

explanation.surface: A slap on the face, or on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a figurative slap in the face; as an adjective the word describes a short upturned nose.

clue.text: Double royalty for amusing author

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: An author receives a double payment of royalties for being funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royalty' suggests payments to an author, but the phrase gives two kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian nonsense poet behind The Owl and the Pussycat, famed for comic limericks.

clue.text: Know arm is broken? Give a hand

indicators.note: when something is broken its pieces are rearranged, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who knows their arm is fractured asks for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a hand' looks like a request for help, but 'a hand' is the definition and 'Give' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker or labourer, as in farmhand.

clue.text: Walks pompously in braces

definitions.meaning: structural supports that hold parts of a frame apart

explanation.surface: Someone parades self-importantly wearing trouser supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'braces' suggests the British word for trouser suspenders, but it means the supporting bars in a framework.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to swagger; the noun names rods bracing a structure.

clue.text: Old goat settled on the up-line

parts.note: sat means settled down in a seat
line gives RY, the railway abbreviation; written upwards in a down entry it reads YR

explanation.surface: An elderly goat sitting beside a railway track heading to London.
explanation.walkthrough: An up line is a railway line toward London; here it means RY (railway) written going up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland god of Greek myth, part goat, also a byword for a lecherous older man.

clue.text: Drab lyric mostly rewritten in humorously colourful language

indicators.note: writing again lets the letters be set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A dull song is mostly reworked into funny, vivid wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LYRIC to LYRI; 'rewritten' then rearranges DRAB with LYRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, crude jokes and talk, vulgar but amusing, as in bawdy humour.

clue.text: Strip of wood used by Indians, primarily

definitions.text: Strip of wood used by Indians, primarily

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word Indians is used

explanation.surface: A wooden strip used chiefly by people in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A long iron-bound bamboo stick used as a weapon, especially by Indian police.

clue.text: Destroy container

definitions.meaning: informal sense of ruin, as in dashing someone's hopes
a bowl or plate for food

explanation.surface: Smash the receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the verb means to ruin; the noun is a vessel for serving food.

clue.text: E.g. hunter's brief retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a remit is a brief, the area of responsibility given to someone

explanation.surface: A huntsman takes a short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief retreat' looks like a short holiday, but 'brief' is a noun meaning REMIT, which 'retreat' turns round. A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a watch with a protective cover, and a watch is an example of a clock or timekeeper.

clue.text: Repeatedly included in quite a moderate amateur side

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words, and occur there twice over

explanation.surface: A fairly mediocre amateur side.
explanation.walkthrough: The run appears twice: in quiTE A Moderate and again in moderaTE AMateur, hence 'Repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, eleven players on a field.

clue.text: Drink taken later deranges a mad bunch bent on destruction

indicators.note: the drink comes after the other part of the answer
mad suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink taken later sends someone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deranges' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'mad' is the indicator. The herd of pigs in the Gospels rushed into the sea after demons entered them.
explanation.definitionFit: In the New Testament, demons cast into a herd of pigs at Gadara drove them over a cliff to destruction.
